decisions.reason: As a classic handle line it remains close to the firm's core metal-hardware know-how and easy to support, but its mature and less strategic profile makes portfolio pruning somewhat more plausible than for newer focus areas.

This handle family builds directly on established design, engineering and certification capabilities, so the firm can keep learning from and incrementally improving it at relatively low knowledge risk.

The design is still close to the firm's existing competences, yet as a more specific single design rather than a broader family it is more exposed to rationalisation if demand or differentiation proves limited.
A multi-model lever-handle family fits the firm's broad system portfolio and absorptive capacity in architectural fittings, which favors retention unless it is clearly cannibalised by other ranges.

The electronic access system matches the firm's strategic move toward digital building organisation and draws strongly on its in-house R&D and adjacent access-control knowledge, so continued investment is very likely.
